subject: Critical Thinking
title: Thomas Kuhn: How Scientific Revolutions Actually Work
description: A short lesson to help you apply Thomas Kuhn: How Scientific Revolutions Actually Work.

hook.text: Science doesn't progress smoothly. It lurches: long periods of normal work, then sudden, violent revolutions.

buildup.text: 'The Structure of Scientific Revolutions': science works within paradigms – shared frameworks that define problems.

discovery.text: Normal science: solving puzzles within the paradigm. But anomalies accumulate.

twist.text: Paradigm shifts aren't just adding new facts – they change what counts as a fact.

climax.text: Examples: Newtonian → Einsteinian physics, miasma → germ theory, geocentric → heliocentric.

punchline.text: Science changes not only by adding facts, but by replacing the lenses used to read them.

quiz.question: What is a 'paradigm shift' according to Thomas Kuhn?
options: A small update to a theory
A revolutionary change in the fundamental framework through which science views and interprets the world
Switching to a new lab technique

details.summary: Thomas Kuhn argued that science does not progress through steady accumulation but through revolutionary paradigm shifts. Normal science works within an accepted framework until anomalies force a crisis and a new paradigm replaces the old one.
details.whyItMatters: Kuhn showed that the social structure of science influences what counts as knowledge, challenging the idealized view of science as purely objective inquiry.
takeaways: Science alternates between normal periods and revolutionary ones
Anomalies accumulate until they trigger paradigm crisis
The scientific community's social dynamics shape progress

faq.question: What is the difference between normal science and revolutionary science?
faq.answer: Normal science solves puzzles within the current paradigm, refining and extending accepted theories. Revolutionary science occurs when unsolvable anomalies force the adoption of an entirely new framework that redefines the field's questions and methods.

faq.question: Does Kuhn's theory mean scientific knowledge is not objective?
faq.answer: Kuhn's view is more nuanced. He argues that paradigms shape what scientists observe and consider important, making objectivity more complex than naive realism suggests. Critics debate whether this undermines or merely complicates claims of scientific objectivity.
